flashcards.front: What is the equation for a line through (x0, y0) with slope m?
flashcards.explanation: This is the standard point-slope form of a linear equation used to define the tangent line.

flashcards.front: What is the slope of the tangent line to y = f(x) at x0?
flashcards.back: The derivative of f at x0, denoted f'(x0).
flashcards.explanation: The derivative represents the instantaneous slope of the function at a specific point.

flashcards.front: How is the tangent line defined using secant lines?
flashcards.back: It is the limit of secant lines PQ as Q approaches P.
flashcards.explanation: This limit process allows us to calculate the slope of the tangent line analytically.

flashcards.front: What is the y-coordinate of point P on the curve y = f(x) at x0?
flashcards.explanation: The y-coordinate is simply the function evaluated at the given x-value.
